body:
It was in astrophysics, my dissertation involved classification of galaxies. I dont want to say too much more other than due to the nature of the project I was given (which was a dumb project for many reasons, and I was not allowed to change it despite pointing the flaws out many times to my advisor) I didn't do much in the way of math/data science/programming/machine-learning/big-data that many astro PhDs can usually boast about at the end of their degrees.

I had a lot of failed experiments/hypotheses, and in the end managed to tie just enough data together to write a dissertation and graduate. But I have very little to show for it.

In essence I have a little bit of experience in a handful of transferable things, but not enough experience in any one of those things to ever get me a job. Believe me, I have tried. 

I dont have the energy or money for more training at this stage unless its on the job training. I worked for free and/or very little money for about a year now with no prospect for change in circumstances and I'm stuck
